title: Ham, cheddar and Bramley breakfast loaf

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything here is a plain kitchen staple: flour, eggs, milk, oil, ham, cheddar, mustard, a Bramley and sage, with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every item is an everyday line at Tesco or similar, at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a loaf tin, bowl, jug and grater, and mixing then baking a quick loaf suits a beginner.

works.reason: The batter ratio is typical of a savoury quick bread, 190°C for 50 minutes in a 900g tin is sound, and a sliced loaf feeds four at breakfast.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes covers peeling and grating the apple, chopping the ham and sage, grating the cheese and lining the tin, and 70 minutes is the 50-minute bake plus the 20-minute cool.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used, including the oil for greasing the tin, and nothing appears in the steps that is not listed.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm, make-ahead loaf with a whole grated Bramley suits a December breakfast, and the apple's sharpness is central to the ham and cheese pairing.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English instructions with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling breakfast with ham, cheese, eggs and fruit that a family would happily make again.
